provenance.note: the production schedules are executed with `globalThis.setTimeout` replaced by a recorder, so no wall-clock time passes and the delays are exact; the integration helper is read from the reference's own syntax tree instead, because intercepting its sleep would mean rewriting its import

wait_schedules.name: defaults
wait_schedules.note: no options at all: minSleep 10 ms, maxSleep 10000 ms, increaseFactor 50 ms

wait_schedules.name: vlei_issuance
wait_schedules.note: singlesig-vlei-issuance and delegation-multisig: a 1000 ms floor that really does bind

wait_schedules.name: multisig_join
wait_schedules.note: multisig-join: an equal floor and ceiling, which flattens the curve to a constant

wait_schedules.name: immediate
wait_schedules.note: an operation already finished on the first poll, which never sleeps

wait_schedules.name: long_run
wait_schedules.note: far enough for the ceiling to bind and the delay to stop growing

integration_helper.note: read from the reference's own syntax tree by its own TypeScript, not executed: driving it would mean rewriting its `timers/promises` import to intercept the sleep, which would change the code under test

server_guidance_scan.note: the pinned tree is searched for every spelling of the header and of a rate-limit status; a zero count is what makes the absence evidence rather than an assertion

production_polling_is_unbounded.note: `Operations.wait` polls in a `while (true)` with no deadline and no attempt cap, so an operation the agent never finishes hangs the caller forever; only an AbortSignal can end it, and only the caller can supply one
production_polling_is_unbounded.rust_decision: a policy is bounded by construction: a maximum attempt count is required and a total deadline is optional but checked, so a schedule always terminates

production_abort_is_checked_after_sleepi.note: `Operations.wait` passes no signal to its `setTimeout`, then checks the signal only after waking, so aborting during a sleep still waits out the full delay — up to the 10000 ms default ceiling — before anything notices
production_abort_is_checked_after_sleepi.rust_decision: cancellation is dropping the future, so a dropped retry stops inside the sleep; the sleep itself is the cancellation point

helper_abort_differs_from_production.note: the integration helper passes its signal into `setTimeout(delay, undefined, { signal })`, so its sleep really is interruptible; the production loop does not — the two disagree about what aborting means
helper_abort_differs_from_production.rust_decision: one behaviour, at the one place a wait happens

no_jitter_anywhere.note: the delay is a pure function of the attempt number, so every client that starts a long-running operation at the same moment retries at the same moments forever
no_jitter_anywhere.rust_decision: jitter is applied by default (`Jitter::Equal`, a delay in [d/2, d]); `Jitter::None` exists to reproduce this schedule exactly and for deterministic tests

server_guidance_is_ignored.note: no file in the pinned tree mentions `Retry-After` in any spelling, so a server asking to be left alone for thirty seconds is retried on the client's own schedule regardless
server_guidance_is_ignored.rust_decision: a valid `Retry-After` in delta-seconds overrides the computed delay, bounded by a configured ceiling so a hostile or mistaken server cannot park a client indefinitely

min_sleep_cannot_bind_at_the_defaults.note: the floor is compared against `2**0 * increaseFactor`, which is already 50 ms at the defaults, so the documented 10 ms minimum can never take effect unless a caller raises it — as the vLEI suites do, to 1000 ms
min_sleep_cannot_bind_at_the_defaults.rust_decision: the floor is kept as a real parameter and the reference's own schedule is reproduced exactly, floor included

an_equal_floor_and_ceiling_flattens_the_.note: `multisig-join` passes minSleep === maxSleep === 500, which makes the exponential term irrelevant and the schedule constant; it is the only pinned caller that does
an_equal_floor_and_ceiling_flattens_the_.rust_decision: reproduced: the same floor and ceiling produce the same constant schedule

the_ceiling_binds_and_the_delay_stops_gr.note: at the defaults the delay doubles from 50 ms until it reaches the 10000 ms ceiling and then stays there
the_ceiling_binds_and_the_delay_stops_gr.rust_decision: same, with the doubling computed on checked integers so a long-lived poll cannot overflow the shift

every_failure_is_retried_by_the_helper.note: `retry.ts` retries whatever the callback threw — a network fault, a 400, a programming error — and the integration suites wrap whole credential lookups in it, so a permanently wrong request is repeated until the 10000 ms timeout elapses
every_failure_is_retried_by_the_helper.rust_decision: an outcome is classified before it is retried, and a method HTTP does not define as idempotent is not retried at all unless the caller widens the scope explicitly
